question: A 55-year-old asthmatic patient goes to the ER with an exacerbation. One hour after the administration of supplemental oxygen and two nebulizations of salbutamol the patient does not improve. On examination, he breathed at 42 rpm with supraclavicular drainage and presented disseminated inspiratory and expiratory wheezing. The peak flow has dropped from 310 to 220 L / min. A gasometry extracted with oxygen at 28% shows a pO2 of 54 mmHg and a pCO2 of 35 mmHg. Which of the following attitudes seems LESS indicated?

options.opc: Nebulize ipratropium bromide together with salbutamol every 20 minutes.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Asthmatic exacerbation" -> "Supplemental oxygen and salbutamol nebulizations" -> "No improvement in symptoms" -> "Increased respiratory rate (42 rpm)" -> "Supraclavicular retractions and wheezing" -> "Decreased peak flow (310 to 220 L/min)" -> "Gasometry: pO2 54 mmHg, pCO2 35 mmHg" -> 80% CHAIN: "Supplemental oxygen and salbutamol nebulizations" -> "No improvement in symptoms" -> "Gasometry: pO2 54 mmHg, pCO2 35 mmHg" -> "Indication for further interventions" -> 85% CHAIN: "Gasometry: pO2 54 mmHg, pCO2 35 mmHg" -> "Hypoxemia and normal pCO2" -> "Indication for non-invasive mechanical ventilation" -> 90% CHAIN: "Gasometry: pO2 54 mmHg, pCO2 35 mmHg" -> "Indication for systemic corticosteroids (methylprednisolone)" -> "80%" CHAIN: "Gasometry: pO2 54 mmHg, pCO2 35 mmHg" -> "Indication for intravenous magnesium" -> 75% CHAIN: "Gasometry: pO2 54 mmHg, pCO2 35 mmHg" -> "Indication for ipratropium bromide nebulization with salbutamol" -> "70%" CHAIN: "Gasometry: pO2 54 mmHg, pCO2 35 mmHg" -> "Indication for increasing oxygen flow" -> 80%
